## ✨ Added

- Per-container backup-folder selection: choose exactly which mapped folders to back up, plus custom paths under the host mount.
- Backup notifications via Webhook (Generic JSON, Discord, Slack, Gotify, ntfy), Matrix, or Healthchecks.io. Policy: never / on failure / always.
- Stop other containers during a backup: name dependent containers (e.g. a database) to stop while this one is backed up and start again afterwards, over the Docker API (no scripts). They always restart, even if the backup fails.
- Plain export (tar + xml), per container: an Export button writes a browsable, tool-free copy next to your repo, `<name>.tar.gz` of the backup folders plus the Unraid `<name>.xml` template (same idea as the Appdata Backup plugin). restic stays the engine; the export is an extra, unencrypted convenience copy.
- Delete individual backups: a Delete button on each snapshot (containers, VMs, flash) removes just that backup.
- Repository maintenance (Settings > Integrity & maintenance), per domain: Verify (`restic check`), Unlock (clear a stale lock left by an interrupted run, the "repository is already locked" fix), and Prune (reclaim space from deleted backups).

- Adds the third backup domain, Unraid flash backup: BombVault now backs up and restores Docker containers, KVM/libvirt VMs and the Unraid USB flash, feature-complete across all three domains.
- Back up the whole flash (`/boot`) via restic: Unraid OS, license, array config (`super.dat`), shares, network, SSH and plugin config, everything on the USB. Incremental + deduplicated like the other domains.
- Safe restore: a flash snapshot is extracted to a folder (`/mnt/user/bombvault/flash-restore` by default) that you then copy onto a fresh USB. The live, running `/boot` is never overwritten, so flash restore cannot leave the server unbootable.
- Flash tab in the sidebar (revealed when you enable Flash under Settings > Domains): one-click "Back up flash now", a snapshot list, and per-snapshot extract-restore that shows exactly where the recovered files landed.
- Scheduled flash backups run automatically when a Flash schedule is set (per-domain everyN due-gate, scoped to flash).
- New mount: the template now mounts the whole flash (`/boot` to `/host/boot`, replacing the narrower templates-only mount it subsumes). Re-import the template (or add the mount) to enable Flash backup.

- Off-site backups (rclone + SMB/NFS): a Backup Path can now be a remote restic backend, `rclone:<remote>:<bucket>/path` for cloud (Backblaze B2, S3, Google Drive, ...). Paste your rclone config under Settings > Off-site (rclone); it is stored AES-256-GCM-encrypted (APP_KEY) and written to a `0600` file only for restic-to-rclone to read.
- SMB/CIFS & NFS need no rclone: mount the network share on Unraid and point a Backup Path at it.
- Local and remote repos are auto-initialised on first use.
- Retention (Settings > Retention): keep-last / keep-daily / keep-weekly / keep-monthly. After each successful backup, restic prunes older snapshots to the policy (per-item, via restic's host+paths grouping). All zero = keep everything (off, the default).
- File-level restore (containers): expand a snapshot's Files, filter, and restore an individual file or folder back to its original location; recover one broken config file without restoring the whole appdata. The include path is validated to stay within the backup mount.

- Integrity checks (Settings > Integrity): run `restic check` per domain (Containers / VMs / Flash) to verify a repository's structure and metadata are intact. Friendly "no backups yet" when a repo hasn't been created; bounded by a timeout.
- Pre/post-backup hooks (per container): each container can run a pre-backup and post-backup shell command (Containers > a container's Backup hooks). Commands run inside the container (`sh -c`).
- Pre runs while the container is still up, e.g. `mysqldump`/`pg_dump` into appdata so a consistent dump is included in the backup; a failing pre-hook aborts the backup (no inconsistent snapshot).
- Post runs after the container is back up (e.g. notify a webhook); its failure is logged but never fails the backup.
- Hooks are command execution by design; they run only inside the named, validated container and are gated by the same auth as every other action, with no new capability over the Docker socket BombVault already uses.

## 🎨 Design

- Collapsible folder tree for file-level restore: expand/collapse like a file manager instead of one long flat list.
- Live progress bar across the full width at the bottom of each card.
- New white-framed logo in the sidebar and browser tab.

## ⚡ Improved

- This release bundles a wave of UX, reliability and quality-of-life improvements onto the feature-complete 1.x line, most of them driven by detailed Unraid forum testing.
- Huge thanks to @manilx on the Unraid forums for the relentless testing, the clear bug reports and the sharp feature ideas; a big part of this release exists because of that feedback.
- VM live backups are reliable and never silently shut a VM down: a live backup that hits a leftover BombVault snapshot overlay from a previously interrupted run now auto-commits that overlay and continues live; if a live snapshot genuinely cannot be taken it fails with a clear message and leaves the VM running (use the explicit "graceful" method if you want a shutdown backup). The per-VM method tooltip now spells out graceful = shutdown vs live = no downtime.
- Backups never auto-create a share: BombVault no longer creates `/mnt/user/bombvault` at first run (which Unraid turned into an undeletable share); the backup folder is created only when the first backup actually runs.
- Clearer status for data-less containers: a container with no data folders reports "Config only" instead of a plain "Done".
- The dashboard shows which container/VM each run was for, and the error on failure.
- Same-repo operations are serialised, so a backup, prune or unlock can never run over each other.

- Flash backup needs the `/boot` mount above; without it the app reports a clear "flash not mounted" message instead of failing obscurely.
- Restore writes to `<flash repo>-restore` next to your flash repo path; it is a recovery staging folder, not a live overwrite.
- Container and VM backup/restore are unchanged from v1.0.0.

Image: `ghcr.io/junkerderprovinz/bombvault:1.1.0` (also `:1`, `:1.1`, `:latest`), multi-arch (amd64 + arm64).

- CI boot smoke-test: CI now boots the built image and curls `/api/health` before pushing `:latest` / the release tag, so a non-booting image can never reach the registry.
- Off-site, retention and file-level restore are all configured in the app; no template change is required for this release.
- `rclone` ships in the image already; no new dependency.

- Credits: BombVault's core idea, one-click backup and automatic re-install of Docker containers, comes from [VolumeVault](https://github.com/Darkdragon14/VolumeVault) by [@Darkdragon14](https://github.com/Darkdragon14) (Apache-2.0). BombVault is an independent Go + restic rewrite that extends the concept to VMs and the Unraid flash. See the README Credits section.
- Hardening: container exec (hook) output is read through a capped reader; JSON request bodies are size-limited (1 MiB), both from the pre-release security audit (no blockers found).
- No template change for this release; everything is configured in-app.

Image: `ghcr.io/junkerderprovinz/bombvault:1.3.0` (also `:1`, `:1.3`, `:latest`), multi-arch (amd64 + arm64).

## 🐛 Fixed

- Run history could fail to load ("Failed to load runs"): an interrupted run left a record the history could not read; it loads again (no database reset, it was never corruption), and interrupted runs are tidied up on startup.
- "Failed to load backups" now self-heals a stale repository lock (clears it and retries).
- Containers with no appdata no longer error; they are backed up as a definition-only backup (recreated on restore).
- VM live snapshots skip cdrom / read-only disks instead of failing on them.

- Saving settings no longer wipes the auth password: the settings save rebuilt the row without the password hash (and would also have dropped the new rclone config); separately-managed secrets are now preserved across a settings save.

Image: `ghcr.io/junkerderprovinz/bombvault:1.2.0` (also `:1`, `:1.2`, `:latest`), multi-arch (amd64 + arm64).
